newsitem.title: UK: Dollar firm, Euro shares/Wall St advance.
newsitem.headline: Dollar firm, Euro shares/Wall St advance.

text.p: The dollar surged to its highest level against the yen for more than four years on Monday, while stock markets on both sides of the Atlantic advanced, putting recent pessimism behind them.
Oil prices recovered a little after plunging nearly nine percent last week but traders said further losses were likely in the short term due to heavy supplies.
Gold also regained some lost ground as delays in Russian shipments boosted precious metals generally.
On the currency market, the dollar, adding to earlier gains in Asian business, progressed by around 1.50 yen and three pfennigs from last week's late levels.
Prospects of further increases in American interest rates and comments by Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin that a firm dollar was good for the U.S. economy helped give the U.S. currency a solid boost.
"It seems fairly plain that there will be at least one more rise in U.S. interest rates at a time when real rates in Japan are set to turn negative," said Julian Fisher, economist at Daiwa Europe.
Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer helped the dollar along, too, saying there was no reason for concern about the currency market, including the dollar.
"The fact that Tietmeyer didn't refer to dollar levels was definitely a dollar-buying factor," said Junpei Yamamoto, head of foreign exchange at Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi in London.
But traders said the market would be on the alert for central bank intervention, verbal or otherwise, to stop the dollar rising too much.
Analysts said dollar bulls had been encouraged by the lack of acrimony during Rubin's visit to Japan last week when he again criticised Japan's ballooning trade surplus.

The dollar advanced well above 1.70 marks to a three-week high against the German currency, helped by progress by European Union finance ministers towards launching the single euro currency, which would replace the mark.

The German currency also weakened against other European units due to renewed optimism on European economic and monetary union (EMU) being launched as planned in 1999. It slipped to 984.90 lire from 990.83 late on Friday and to 84.44 pesetas from 84.52.

But some uncertainty seemed to remain -- enough to make German Finance Minster Theo Waigel counter press reports that he had softened his stance on the budget deficit criterion for EMU. He insisted that he opposed looser interpretation of the rule.
The pound, meanwhile, rose above its old floor of 2.7780 marks in the European exchange rate mechanism for the first time since it left the system in September 1992, hitting a late 2.7815 marks.

European stock markets were already in a positive mood before the New York market reopened higher, celebrating a recovery on Wall Street on Friday and the strength of the dollar -- good news for Europe's exporters.
By the end, Frankfurt had gained more than three percent, Paris over two percent and London, Europe's biggest stock market, a more moderate 0.85 percent.

On Wall Street, the Dow Jones industrial average was around 49 points or 0.76 percent higher by 1600 GMT, roughly matching the 48.72 points it reclaimed on Friday with help from bonds, a rally in the high technology sector and merger interest.
"The rally is being led by bonds. There is a feeling that the worst of the selling is behind us," said Guy Truicko, portfolio manager at Unity Management in New York.
The German share market confounded expectations to book sharp gains, helped by higher bonds. Traders said rumours of the death of the bull run seemed somewhat exaggerated right now.
"What we are seeing is the typical short squeeze," said one Frankfurt trader.

London shares ended the first day of the new British tax year higher, shadowing Wall Street, but concern about interest rate rises was likely to cap advances in the FTSE 100 index, dealers and strategists said.
"We've had a predictable bounce today but not a convincing bounce," one senior dealer said. "People are afraid that if U.S. rates keep going up, the Dow will head lower, dragging the FTSE with it."
French shares closed sharply higher as market sentiment changed and Wall Street and the dollar revived, dealers said.
The Dutch, Italian, Spanish, Swedish and Swiss bourses were also up around two percent or more.
CURRENCIES AT THE EUROPEAN CLOSE
The dollar was quoted around 1.7082 marks and 125.73 yen, up from 1.6768 and 124.23 in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT THE EUROPEAN CLOSE
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index ended up 35.1 points or 0.83 percent at 4,271.7.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended bourse floor trade up 67.95 points or 2.09 percent at 3,312.88. In later electronic trade, the IBIS DAX index finished at 3,342.77 for a gain of 3.32 percent.
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed 54.34 points or 2.16 percent ahead at 2,572.31.
OIL/PRECIOUS METALS
London futures for benchmark North Sea Brent blend crude had gained 42 cents to $18.10 a barrel by 1600 GMT after last week's $1.70 slide and losses of $6.50 so far this year.
Gold ended London trading at $349.30 an ounce, just above the afternoon fix of $349 and ahead of the previous London close of $347.45. Silver added seven cents to $4.80 and platinum $4 to $367.
